column1: # fe-drops.tsv -- MONSTER DROPS (OURS, 2026-09-12). SE never shipped a drop table
# (fet_npc_type has no drop column; the image and dat.pak name none), so every row
# here is sourced from the 2006 fewiki `Monster` page (RoD, 2006-04/05) or its Quest /
# Consumables pages, mapped to item ids (fe-fet-items.tsv) and fet monster names.
# family  = an fnmatch pattern on the monster's fet name (m["name"]): Goblin_Novice,
#           *Orc*, Harpy* ... the wiki's levels do not match fet's, so key by family.
# lv_min / lv_max = the monster's fet level band (0..999 = any).
# sex     = M / F / - : armour rows exist once per sex (model_m or model_f only);
#           the roll only offers the killer's own. Checked against the item table at
#           load -- a row naming an item the client does not have is REFUSED (a null
#           item record is the known client crash).
# rate_ppm = an independent roll per row, parts per million. The rates are CHOSEN --
#           no 2006 rate survives. Operator 2026-09-12: "Agree with your drop rate
#           The wiki's bold ("rare") items are the rare rows. One item per kill: the
